clue.text: If bowled over, pant about wife, buzzy creature drawn to wild flowers (7, two words)

definitions.text: buzzy creature drawn to wild flowers

indicators.note: something bowled over is knocked head over heels, so the little word before it is turned back to front

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for pant wraps around the single letter for wife

parts.note: to pant is to gasp for breath
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A cricketer knocked flat lies panting about his wife while a bee drifts towards the wildflowers.
explanation.walkthrough: The wife's letter sits just after the first letter of pant's synonym. The wild flowers are those of the fig, whose tiny blossoms are concealed inside the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Fig wasps are tiny insects that pollinate the concealed flowers of wild fig trees, laying eggs inside them.

clue.text: No moderate rising like this should be restricted by firm

indicators.note: being restricted by something means being hemmed in by it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: firm, as in fixed fast or held fast

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Latin sic, thus, so written, as used in quotations

explanation.surface: A centrist politician's rise ought to be kept in check by a company, so the clue suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company; it is the adjective meaning fixed. Sic is the Latin tag printed after a quoted error to show it was written thus.
explanation.definitionFit: A fascist is an extremist of the authoritarian right, the opposite of a political moderate.

clue.text: I see wayward Tory was in debt, holding on, unworldly

indicators.note: holding means gripping something within, so the debt word wraps around the little word for on

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: wayward means straying out of line, so the letters of the party word wander into a new order

parts.note: V is short for vide, Latin for see
taken as written, then rearranged
someone in debt owed money
RE means on or about, as in a memo heading

explanation.surface: Someone observes a Conservative who strayed and ran up debts while clinging on.
explanation.walkthrough: V for 'see' comes from Latin vide, used in footnotes. 'Tory' looks like the subject of 'was in debt', but it is only anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An ivory tower is a place of sheltered academic seclusion, so the adjective describes someone remote from practical everyday life.

clue.text: Love entering little wood, a pleasurable experience

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the love letter goes into the small wood

parts.note: a grove is a small group of trees
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Romance blossoming in a copse makes for a delightful time.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, a groove is something thoroughly enjoyable, as in the phrase 'in the groove'.

clue.text: Fairground ride offered by e.g. Disney — almost nothing

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of it, so the last letter of the word for nothing is dropped

parts.note: Walt Disney, the animator, is an example of a Walt
zero is nothing

explanation.surface: A theme-park attraction from Disney that costs next to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'e.g.' marks Disney as one example of the forename WALT.
explanation.definitionFit: A waltzer is a fairground ride of spinning cars on an undulating track, whirling riders round as in a dance.

clue.text: Well, hello! Here's one who rode into battle

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring or well
an informal greeting

explanation.surface: A cheery greeting introducing a warrior who went into combat on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well, hello!' reads as one exclamation, but Well is a noun here: a spring of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A spahi was a cavalryman, originally in the Ottoman army and later in French Algerian regiments.

clue.text: Want surplus proprietary bags

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it in a sack, so one word holds the other within it

parts.note: Pty is the abbreviation for proprietary, as in company names like Pty Ltd
over means left over, in excess

explanation.surface: A company with branded goods craves more than it needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Want as a noun means lack of the necessities of life, the same as being poor.

clue.text: 'Source' of tropical disease — I'll escape recurrent attack

indicators.note: recurrent suggests running back, so the word for attack is read in the backwards direction
the letter I gets out and leaves, so it is removed from the word

parts.note: to assail is to attack

explanation.surface: Someone hoping to escape repeated bouts of a fever caught in the tropics.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversing ASSAIL gives LIASSA; the I then drops out. 'Source' is in quotes because the place gives its name to the fever rather than causing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassa in Nigeria is the village where Lassa fever, a viral haemorrhagic disease of West Africa, was first identified.

clue.text: Bikini maybe for hiding everything? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: hiding means concealing something within, so one word is tucked inside another
this swaps the roles just described, so the word that seemed to be hidden does the concealing

parts.note: all means everything
for and to are interchangeable in phrases like 'a reason for/to'

explanation.surface: Is a bikini meant to hide everything? Far from it.
explanation.walkthrough: The swimwear picture hides a place: Bikini is the Pacific island where nuclear bombs were tested, and the swimsuit was named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikini is a Pacific coral island, an example of a ring-shaped reef enclosing a lagoon, used for nuclear tests.

clue.text: Houses (semi) I'll occupy through freehold possession in Edinburgh

indicators.note: to occupy is to take up residence inside, so the letter goes within the shortened houses
semi means half, so only the latter half of the word for houses is used

parts.note: the second half of the six-letter word
taken as written
in can mean through or by means of
surface padding: the contraction only makes the sentence grammatical

explanation.surface: Half of a pair of semi-detached houses, which I will live in, held outright in the Scottish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'll' of I'll is just grammar. Chambers lists this as a variant of sasine, the Scots legal term, hence Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: Seisin is the legal term for possession of land held freehold; in Scots law the same idea is sasine.

clue.text: Specially geared up, heading off Aunt Ann pedals furiously

indicators.note: with its heading taken off, the word loses its first letter
pedalling furiously suggests wild churning, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the first letter is removed
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An aunt on a bicycle with special gears, pedalling away furiously.
explanation.walkthrough: The bicycle picture makes 'geared up' read as being ready; it describes a particular gearing system.
explanation.definitionFit: Sun-and-planet gearing has one toothed wheel orbiting a central one, as in Watt's steam engines and some bicycle hubs.

clue.text: Fit? Run in that contest

indicators.note: in that means placed inside the thing just mentioned, the word for fit

parts.note: an ague is a fit of fever or shivering
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A question about fitness, then a suggestion to enter a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit?' looks like an adjective about health; it is a noun, a bout of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: To contest a point is to dispute it, which is to argue about it.

clue.text: One preparing dossier for committee, sympathy and pity returning

parts.note: rapport is a sympathetic understanding between people

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for pity is read backwards

parts.note: rue is an old word for pity or regret

explanation.surface: A committee's report writer shows understanding and compassion when they come back.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapporteur is the person appointed by a committee to draw up and present its report on proceedings.

clue.text: Pull (as M. Antony did his countrymen?), with loose rambling

definitions.text: Pull (as M. Antony did his countrymen?)

indicators.note: rambling means wandering aimlessly, so the letters stray into another order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Mark Antony tugs at his fellow Romans with a loose, rambling speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb means to pull by the ears; Antony began his funeral speech 'Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears'.
explanation.definitionFit: Soole is an old dialect verb meaning to pull someone by the ears, which Antony figuratively did to his audience.

clue.text: How released spring goes, in being embraced by ladies?

indicators.note: being embraced means being held within someone's arms, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: bog is British slang for a toilet, and the ladies is a women's toilet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A playful picture of a spring bouncing into a group of women's arms.
explanation.walkthrough: The ladies here is the women's public toilet, and bog is British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: The word imitates the twanging sound made by a compressed spring suddenly let go.

clue.text: Etch squiggles in reverse of necklace — an ingenious idea

indicators.note: the reverse of a word is that word read from its end to its beginning
in places the rearranged letters inside the turned-round necklace

parts.note: a torc is a Celtic metal neck ring

indicators.note: squiggles are wiggly scribbles, so the letters of etch get twisted around

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Scratching swirly patterns on the back of a necklace — a clever notion.
explanation.walkthrough: TCHE goes inside CROT, between O and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A crotchet, besides a musical note, is a whimsical fancy or odd conceit, here called an ingenious idea.

clue.text: Rope for hoisting tackle back, inlet abandoned

indicators.note: back means going in the opposite direction, so the tackle word is read backwards

parts.note: a rig is a set of tackle or gear

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Sailors haul back their gear on a rope after leaving a small bay behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A girtline is a rope rove through a block at a masthead, used on ships to hoist rigging or men aloft.

clue.text: Mount section ready for driving

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for section
in golf a ball is teed up ready to be driven off

explanation.surface: Put together a piece of a vehicle prepared for the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driving' suggests cars; it is a golf drive off the tee.
explanation.definitionFit: A steed is a horse for riding, and a mount is the animal one rides.

clue.text: Afghani maybe cutting initial pressure with gold in unusual furnace

indicators.note: cutting the initial means chopping off the first letter, here the one for pressure

parts.note: the Pathans (Pashtuns) are a people of Afghanistan, so an Afghani may be one
P is the symbol for pressure
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An Afghan working a strange furnace eases the pressure while adding gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Afghani' could be the currency, but here it is a person from Afghanistan.
explanation.definitionFit: An athanor was the self-feeding digesting furnace of the alchemists, which kept a steady heat for long periods.

clue.text: What'll be showing the latest thing in taste?

definitions.text: What'll be showing the latest thing in taste?

indicators.note: in places the word for latest thing inside the word for taste

parts.note: to try food is to taste it
the end is the last thing of all

explanation.surface: A question about what will look fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: something that shows the latest thing in taste is fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendy means following the newest fashions, so it shows what is currently in vogue.

clue.text: Sticking to principles I teach revised Latin

indicators.note: something revised has been reworked, so these letters are put in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
L is the abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: A principled teacher who updates the Latin course.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ethical means acting according to moral rules, which is keeping to one's principles.

clue.text: Sectarian I eyed askance taking in OT book

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing inside, so the rearranged letters hold the book abbreviation
to look askance is to look sideways, so the letters are knocked askew

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
Ez is the abbreviation for Ezra, a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A member of a sect glances sideways at someone reading a biblical book.
explanation.walkthrough: EZ goes in after the Y of YIDEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yezidis are a Kurdish religious sect, so a Yezidee is a member of that faith.

clue.text: Accessory essential for whippet or retriever?

indicators.note: the essence of a phrase is its inside, so the answer lies within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of whippet, all of or and the start of retriever

explanation.surface: A question about a necessary item of kit for a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is also apt for dogs: it is a ring on a collar for attaching a lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A torret, variant of terret, is a ring on a harness or dog collar, a small fitting or accessory.

clue.text: Energy chronic failure summoned up to mend at last?

indicators.note: in a down clue, being summoned up means coming upwards, so the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy
someone who always fails is a loser

explanation.surface: A hopeless failure finally finds the energy to fix things.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is the shoemaker's foot-shaped block, so 'mend at last' is repair work on a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: To resole a shoe is to fit a new sole, a cobbler's repair done on the last.

clue.text: Obstruct end of passage in mining excavation

parts.note: to obstruct is to stop

indicators.note: end of means only the final letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: Blocking off the far end of a tunnel in a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: A stope is a step-like excavation made underground when removing ore from a mine.

clue.text: Methods for investigating sorceress spending money up front

indicators.note: spending something means using it up so it is gone, here the money letter

parts.note: Morgana, Morgan le Fay, the enchantress of Arthurian legend

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of money, which also leads the name

explanation.surface: A witch who pays in advance to look into something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up front' places the lost letter at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Organa is the plural of organon, a system of rules or principles for scientific or philosophical enquiry.

clue.text: Eddy, formerly from Wales, I encountered in southern Spain

indicators.note: being encountered in a place means being found within it, so the pieces sit inside

parts.note: S is short for southern
an old spelling of Welsh
taken as written
E is the international car code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A man named Eddy, once a Welshman, whom I met in Andalucia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eddy' looks like a man's name; it is a whirlpool. WELCH and I go between S and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A swelchie is an Orkney word for a whirlpool, which is a swirling eddy in the sea.

clue.text: P & O ship endlessly transported Persian king

indicators.note: endlessly means with no end, so the last letter of the vessel is cut off
transported means carried away and moved about, so the letters change places

parts.note: taken as written, the shipping line's initials
the final letter is removed

explanation.surface: A shipping line's vessel carried a Persian monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: P&O is a British shipping company; 'transported' fits the cruise picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophi, or Sophy, is the old title of the Safavid shahs of Persia.

clue.text: Where treasure may be found 'engarlanded', in a manner of speaking?

indicators.note: garlands hang around something, so the treasure marker is wrapped inside the word for garlands

parts.note: the garlands are leis, Hawaiian flower wreaths
X marks the spot on a treasure map

explanation.surface: A playful remark that treasure might lie wreathed in flowers, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: One word does double duty: 'engarlanded' gives LEIS and also tells you to put X inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Lexis is the vocabulary or diction of a language or writer, so a manner of speaking.

clue.text: Mystical interpretation? It makes one agog thus — senseless

indicators.note: the answer is itself the instruction: read it as a phrase and it says to place one word within another to make the mystical term

parts.note: ANAGOGE, mystical interpretation, is formed with AGOG placed IN ANE; that placing word is IN
ane is Scots for one
the word to be placed and the pointer back to the instruction, not letters of the answer

explanation.surface: A mystical reading that leaves a person agog — and yet makes no sense.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as the phrase IN ANE, an instruction to put AGOG in ANE, which spells ANAGOGE, the mystical sense of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means empty or silly, lacking sense or meaning.

clue.text: Fish eaten in Melbourne hostelry brought back in again, battered

indicators.note: brought back means returned, so the hostelry word is read backwards
in places the turned hostelry inside the rearranged letters
battered means knocked about, so the letters of the repeated word are beaten into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
an inn is a hostelry

explanation.surface: Fish and chips again at a Melbourne pub, the fish coated in batter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battered' suits the fish supper, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The nannygai is an Australian red sea fish, a food fish caught off the south-east coast.

clue.text: Agency putting pressure on old cinema?

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
Roxy was a common name for cinemas in their heyday

explanation.surface: An organisation leaning on an old picture house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting ... on' places P before ROXY.
explanation.definitionFit: Proxy means the agency of one person acting on behalf of another, as in voting by proxy.

clue.text: Once examined in Nordic briefly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old past tense of scan
second meaning: the abbreviation of Scandinavian

explanation.surface: Something was once looked over in a Scandinavian language, briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: Scand is an archaic past tense of the verb scan, and Scand. is the short form of Scandinavian.

clue.text: Inhale besottedly, taking in image beloved of the Muses?

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing within, so the rearranged letters hold the image
besotted means muddled with drink or love, so the letters are befuddled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
an icon is an image

explanation.surface: Breathing in rapturously, gazing at a picture adored by the goddesses of the arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Helicon in Greece was sacred to the Muses, so something Heliconian belongs to or is dear to them.

clue.text: Superlative broad (not weak, I mean) (5, two words)

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for weak is removed

parts.note: the superlative of wide, a synonym for broad
W is short for weak

explanation.surface: A woman described as the best — not weak, I mean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broad' looks like slang for a woman; it is the adjective wide.
explanation.definitionFit: Id est is Latin for 'that is', abbreviated i.e., used to introduce a clarification, the same as 'I mean'.

clue.text: Boost cause of delayed kick-off?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to expand an economy again
second meaning, read as two words: the referee is behind time

explanation.surface: A match is held up because something needs a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as REF LATE: a football match cannot start until the referee arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: To reflate is to stimulate an economy by increasing the money supply, giving it a boost.
